# 1.2.75 - a notice history, a new corner, and a Class Trial cast chosen per character

One stage on the way to 1.3.0 (E81), released alone: the notices a browser shows are kept in that browser and can be read again in a window of its own, the three corner buttons stand on a new grid, and the owner's decisions DZ4 (the corner), DZ5 and DZ6 change the table (below; DZ1 stays). Most of it was measured in the headless harness, the corner also in Chromium on the glass harness, some only read in the code; none of it was tried in a real Foundry or at a table.

## Before installing

1. **The scene navigation and the macro hotbar are hidden for everybody, a GM included, in every theme** (DZ5; in 1.2.74 a GM still
   saw both). The Scenes tab of Foundry's sidebar stays on a GM's screen in both themes, and scenes are switched from it. **A macro
   you kept on the hotbar is now run from the Macro Directory** in Foundry's sidebar, as are the five macros the repository carries
   (`macros/`; read in the code). Starting a Class Trial during an Eclipse is still refused (DZ1).
2. **A Class Trial open when you update.** The GMs' choice of who takes part was kept per hall token and is now kept per character.
   On the primary GM's browser, when the world loads, the old rows move once to their characters (the first token of a character in
   the hall decides, and the row keeps its season; R500 and a tier-2 test). Nothing is announced, and until it has run the old
   choice is read through the old key (read in the code). The first time a GM opens the Scenes tab or Start the Class Trial they see
   every character with a tick; until a tick is changed, Monokuma and every student a player owns take part. The hall's student
   tokens become temporary (DZ6, below): tokens you placed stay yours; the module makes one for each ticked character that has none
   (never Monokuma's) the next time the table enters the hall, and deletes it when the trial ends. A trial already running keeps the
   hall as it stands until then, unless a tick is changed in the Scenes tab, which stages it at once (read in the code). Not tried
   at a table (LIVE-E81-14 to -20).
3. **Back up the world, and note the version you ran,** so a problem can be traced back. **On The Forge, install from this release's
   manifest URL.**
4. **The history is kept in each browser, not in the world.** It is a client setting written only by the browser that drew the
   cards; nothing is sent to the world or to another user. A player, or a GM, who signs in from a new browser starts with an empty
   history (both read in the code). The limits, as the window says them (`DRPG.Notices.kept` for a player, `DRPG.Notices.gmNote` for
   a GM):
   > Kept in this browser - at most the newest 250, and 40 from any one sender - until a season reset that clears the clock, the incident, this module's cards or the rest of the chat log; a card the module takes back leaves it. When this browser runs short of room, or other accounts' histories on it fill its share, it keeps fewer or stops saving, and the line below says when it stops.
   > Your own history: what this client showed you. Players keep theirs. It keeps at most the newest 150, and 40 from any one sender, until a season reset that clears the clock, the incident, this module's cards or the rest of the chat log, and a card the module takes back leaves it; on a shared computer another account logged in on this browser can read it, so clear it before you hand the computer over. When this browser runs short of room, or other accounts' histories on it fill its share, it keeps fewer or stops saving, and the line below says when it stops.
5. **Settings, keys and texts.** One new setting, `noticeHistory`, hidden and per browser (123 settings registered, 122 at 1.2.74);
   nothing new in the settings window. One new keybinding, "Notice history", with no key bound (bind one in Foundry's Controls);
   `game.drpg.openNotices()` opens the same window. `lang/en.json` goes from 3316 to 3360 strings (48 added, 4 removed, 8 reworded)
   and `lang/pl.json` from 4083 to 4131 (56 added, 8 removed, 8 reworded). Two new texts ask a GM to place a token by hand: the
   Scenes tab row for a ticked Monokuma with no token in the hall ("place one by hand if the trial needs it") and the whisper when
   the trial opens ("place one on the hall's scene by hand"); the whisper about a token a player deleted is reworded the same way. A
   macro may need changing: `game.drpg.trialSceneReport()` lists in `shown` the cast's tokens shown in the hall now, not the ones
   the next entry would show, and has a new field, `made`. The handbooks were updated; the manifest and the Foundry and Daggerheart
   versions are unchanged.

## At the table

### The notice history

- **What it keeps.** Every card the browser draws for the logged-in user: public cards, cards whispered to their owner, a private
  card's words for that player alone, the messenger's previews, the Class Trial's evidence, the day summary, the safeword card and
  the requests that were not carried out; a GM's browser keeps what is addressed to the table or to that GM. It does not keep the
  cards that wait for a GM's answer, other toasts, the bubbles of an open messenger or the suite's cards, and adds nothing from the
  chat log (read in the code).
- **How much, and for how long.** The newest 250 entries for a player and 150 for a GM, and 40 from any one sender; an entry too
  long to keep whole keeps its text without the markup, and a section holds at most four full day summaries. It lasts to a season
  reset that clears the clock, the incident, this module's cards or the rest of the chat log, and **Clear** in the window empties it
  sooner, after asking. A card the module takes back (an incident's opening requests when it moves on, a crisis a GM undoes) leaves
  the history with it; any other deletion from the chat log leaves the entry, marked "Deleted from the chat log". A Reroll or a GM's
  ruling adds "Rerolled" or "Ruled on by the GM" to the entry and does not change what it shows.
- **The window** opens from the button in the notice tile's corner, from the keybinding (read in the code only) or from
  `game.drpg.openNotices()`. It is read-only: one chip per source (seven, from All to Messenger), a search that ignores accents and
  capitals, entries grouped by time of day with older chapters folded, and "Open the conversation" on a messenger entry. A card
  still on screen at a reload is unread after it: the button carries the count and the window a banner. It plays no sound, draws no
  card again and sends nothing (R296).
- **The safeword.** The entry of the public card names nobody and shows no time (R296, scenario 73). A GM's own note (who called it
  and from which room, cut to 120 characters) is kept in that GM's browser and in no player's, also with no time. **Whose name an
  entry carries:** the user who wrote the card (when a GM's session wrote a messenger card for a player, the thread's player); an
  author who is no user of this world is dropped (fix r2-H1; R297).
- **A season reset** that clears the clock, the incident, this module's cards or the rest of the chat log clears every account's
  history of this world, at once in a browser that is open and in any other the next time it loads the world. **A reset with none of
  those four ticked clears no history.**
- **Accounts that share one browser** keep their sections in one value of its storage, so anybody at that browser's console can read
  the others', a killer's cards and a GM's safeword note included (the owner accepted this on 11.10; the GM handbook's section 19
  says so). A login never removes another account's section (a season reset aside). When the storage is full the history gives way
  to the module's other stores: other worlds' histories go first, then the older half of this login's, and for the rest of the
  session it keeps half as many. When the other accounts' histories fill its share, the newcomer's is kept in memory only until its
  page closes (read in the code, not run), and its window says: "This browser could not save the notice history: the notices shown
  from now on are kept only until this page is closed or reloaded." Clear it before you share your screen or hand the computer over.

### The corner of the screen

- **The history button** stands in the bottom-right corner of the notice tile. Under Stained Glass it is there from the world's
  load, with no card on screen too. Under Monokuma Legacy on a desk it stands alone under the clock with no card, and in the corner
  of the lowest card when there is one. On a narrow screen it is there only while a card is on screen; otherwise use the key or the
  API. It closes no card, and the lowest card keeps its last line clear of it (R298, and the sweep below). **"+N" closes every card
  at once except the sticky ones.**
- **The three buttons stand on one grid** in both themes: the chat on top at 66 px, settings (44 px, was 52) on the bottom line and
  the book (44 px, was 40) against the right wall, every two neighbours 6 px apart (R474 reads the tokens). The GM's roster opens 8
  px over the chat button.
- **A narrow screen** (under 1224 px of width): the notice stack stands 8 px above the corner buttons, between the tool rail and the
  tab rail and no higher than 8 px under the stack of blocks; under 620 px of height it stands beside the buttons on the bottom
  line, 24 px past the one that reaches farthest in, settings (140 px from the wall under Monokuma Legacy, worked out from the
  tokens as R476 reads them, not measured in a browser). What does not fit is parked behind "+N", a card taller than the stack
  scrolls, and the stack is never under 96 px. (Through 1.2.74 it stood on the buttons.)
- **Measured outside Foundry.** `node audit/glass-sweep.mjs` loads the glass harness in Chromium at 22 sizes in both themes (the
  writer's runs, at 57d179c for the corner and 84273d8 for the notice stack; the stylesheets and glass files are unchanged since,
  and no run is recorded at 2c9fe4b). Under Stained Glass 20 of the 22 sizes draw glass; at each, the three corner buttons lie
  inside their own pane, none is hidden and the gaps read 6.00 px; the curtain's self-check reads 0 apart from edgeGaps 16 at
  1280x720, which glass.mjs explains and does not fix. Under Monokuma Legacy no glass is drawn and the three buttons are drawn at
  every size. The notice stack reads clean at all 44 theme-and-size readings. R299 and R111 read the corner inside Foundry; both are
  skipped headless and have not run there (LIVE-E81-02).

### The trial's cast and its tokens

- **Who takes part** is one tick per character, in the Scenes tab ("Who takes part") and in the Start the Class Trial window ("Who
  takes part in this trial"). Start saves only the ticks you changed and Cancel saves nothing; the other doors into the trial use
  the stored choice (read in the code). An unticked character gets no token in the hall and is not moved afterwards.
- **The tokens** (R501, R502, a tier-2 test). When the trial opens, each ticked character with no token of yours in the hall gets
  one, made from its prototype token and linked to the character, where it last stood in the hall (the hall scene remembers it),
  else on a ring round the middle of the scene. One of yours is used instead, and is only shown and hidden, never moved or deleted.
  The module never makes Monokuma's token: a ticked Monokuma with none in the hall, and a token that could not be made, are named to
  the GMs. When the trial ends the tokens the module made are deleted and yours are hidden; only tokens the hall's record names are
  ever deleted. A token left by a browser closed in between is deleted when the primary GM next loads the world with no trial
  running, and a player who deletes a token the module made has it made again at the next opening (both read in the code).
- **End the trial** moves, carries and names only the cast: a student left unticked stays where they stand and nothing names them
  (R436, scenario 41, a tier-2 test). For those who took part, the room you choose and the whispers are as in 1.2.74.

## Changed

- New files: `scripts/notice-history.mjs` (the store and its recorder) and `scripts/notice-history-app.mjs` (the window); the CSS is
  in the existing sheets. `showPopup` gained the options `record`, `source`, `author`, `observe`, `link`, `persist` and
  `fromMessage`; the hooks `drpgThemeApplied`, `drpgStorageFull` and `drpgSecretStored` are new; the case's health has a row for the
  history. `relay-guard.mjs` and `module.json` are unchanged.
- New CSS tokens: `--drpg-launch-*` (seven), `--drpg-stack-foot`, `--drpg-stack-max`, `--drpg-column-max`,
  `--drpg-notices-left/right`, `--drpg-corner*`; `--drpg-book-lane` is gone. `gm-panel.mjs` stamps only the tool rail and the Scenes
  tab.
- The trial: `trial-scene.mjs` gained `stageHall` (the one place the module creates or deletes a hall token) and lost
  `revealTrialTokens`, `hideTrialTokens`, `studentsWithoutHallToken` and `castShownOnEntry`; the record is the hall's flag
  `trialSeats`. `DRPG.TrialScene.missingTokens` is replaced by `notPlaced`, `handPlaced`, `placedByGm`.
- **New tests:** 19 numbered ones (5 in tier 0: R472, R475, R477, R478, R479; 14 in tier 1: R292 to R299, R473, R474, R476, R500 to
  R502), 3 new tier-2 tests (2 replaced), and scenario 73-notice-history in the ci set (24, 23 at 1.2.74). R111 was rewritten under
  its name, R438 and R470 retitled, scenarios 00, 13, 30, 41, 61 and 72 changed. The skip baseline goes from 17 to 18 rows (R299).
  Next free: R503 (R480 to R499 stay unused). `audit/glass-sweep.mjs` is new.

## Known gaps

- Forty-two live checks stand open, items 163 to 204 of the audit's section 9.2: the twenty of 1.2.74 and LIVE-E81-01 to -22. The
  new ones: Foundry's real HTML cleaner against the history's snapshot (-01); the screenshot matrix, with R299 and R111 (-02); F5
  right after a card, since the write on `pagehide` is not measured (-03); the button under Monokuma Legacy (-04) and on a narrow
  screen (-05); a shared browser (-06); touch (-07); a screen reader (-08); Clear in two tabs (-09); scenario 30's probes of
  execution and playback in a real browser (-10); withdraw and delete in Foundry 14, and whether it still strips `deleteAll` (-11);
  sound and the button's accent (-12); the sweep's sizes again in Foundry at a table (-13); the trial's tokens, DZ6's (-14 to -20:
  prototype tokens, the hall's flags, the record's partial write, Daggerheart's cards after a delete, the cost, two GMs, an unticked
  student); a full storage's error (-21); a player deleting their own chat message (-22).
- The window at 393 px and 1366x768 is read only by R299, which has not run. The keybinding is checked only by R296's source clause
  (it reads the registration text); no test presses it and no live check covers a bound key. The settings gear is drawn at 22 px in
  its 44 px button (Q10 belongs to E48). On a client using a light colour scheme the settings and handbooks buttons paint paper
  (found in the harness, not changed). The messenger button's unread badge is cut to a red sliver by the Stained Glass hexagon (also
  in 1.2.74, not changed). These three: measured at C12 and C14 (12.10), not re-measured at 2c9fe4b.
- Found while measuring and there before 1.2.75: under Monokuma Legacy on a desk a long card runs off the screen (3394 px at
  1920x1080, not judged); on a stacked screen the stack stands over the GM PANEL button, which the ceiling does not read. The
  stack's 96 px floor is new in this release and can reach under the blocks. A kept card can lose styling and elements: classes
  built at run time are not on the allowlist, and a card's label, form, button, code and section text is not kept.
- The history: a second tab of the same login may write back entries the give-way dropped (not re-measured after the later fixes);
  give-way writes through the browser storage's `setItem`, not `game.settings.set`; two tabs of one GM keep the safeword note twice,
  and a caller with two tabs keeps the banner twice; at load a card missing from the log cannot be told withdrawn from deleted and
  stays marked deleted; a notice that arrives while a tier-1 test holds the engine is not kept; a user deleted later keeps their
  entries' author id. Read in the code, not run: whom `raiseCard` and `showGmDetail` name.
- Not measured or not tested: the window's chapter folds; Esc against Foundry's own close; Enter and Space on the corner buttons (a
  click is what was measured); the cost of the accessibility sweep now finding the tile at load; the curtain, the fog and the
  remnant ring when a theme switch changes the body's classes; the stack's side insets under Stained Glass headless; the roster's
  place over the chat button beyond 640x360; the `is` attribute rebuild and same-origin images in a kept card (jsdom only). The
  glass sweep needs the history button to exist and reads the bottom card's last line against it, but not where in the corner it
  stands; it reads a stale cut from the `launch` block and the viewport only; C14's scratch sweep read 0 for a turn origin moved by
  40 px (not re-tried on the committed one); its 2.5 s wait and 1.5 px slack were not tried on a slower machine.
- Not in this release: the cleaner fixes of the verification pass (E02; the history cleans a card with its own allowlist on top of
  the module's card cleaner, and the stage plan leaves those fixes to E83); and the body discovery's and a Call's gather still move
  everybody, not only the cast.
